root_cause.method: Read-only probe replaying bootstrap_cgroup_mount admission inside a transient systemd-run unit with the controller's sandbox properties (CapabilityBoundingSet= empty, NoNewPrivileges, ProtectControlGroups, RestrictNamespaces, SystemCallFilter=@system-service, ...); probe file removed and unit collected afterwards.
root_cause.finding_1: open('/proc/1/ns/cgroup') -> PermissionError(13): a capability-less root process cannot follow PID 1's namespace link (ptrace access check). bootstrap_cgroup_mount._namespaces() therefore always fails; open_bootstrap_cgroup_mount() maps it to UnitOperationFailed('fixed cgroup mount admission unavailable'). The same helper is used by the audit peer, commission peer and controller identity checks.
root_cause.finding_2: systemd 257 adds a writable bind mount of the unit's own memory.pressure below the read-only /sys/fs/cgroup (MemoryPressureWatch=auto). _mount_record refuses any mount below /sys/fs/cgroup/, so admission would fail next even with finding 1 fixed.

second_attempt.diagnosis: Sandboxed read-only replays (no files created, verified by find before/after) with the wrapper's exact interpreter flags (-IS), sys.path and dont_write_bytecode: approval at both time bounds, deployment binding, time window, generation, policy-bound capacity and the first-install audit genesis (sequence 0, empty ledger) all pass under the new privileges. Installed-files measurement refuses with 'uncovered negative Python importer cache': CPython caches the executed script path as a None importer entry (probe: '/run/<probe>.py'; controller: '/usr/libexec/azazel/az-activated'), and import_routing accepts None only for /usr/lib/python313.zip or covered directories. An earlier probe's capacity refusal was an artifact of a read-only probe sandbox, and its 'fixed controller main module required' refusal is an artifact of the probe's own __main__.
